title: Effectivity of a normalized DVR tower
statement:
For a tower in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], put
$M=R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}_m M_m$. Then the canonical
counit comparisons give coherent isomorphisms

$$
M\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n
\qquad(n\geq1).
$$

In particular $M$ is derived complete in the sense of
[def-weil-derived-complete]. No constructibility or boundedness
is required for this effectivity assertion.

proof.text: Use the notation of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]: $B_j=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^j)_X$ and $R=\varprojlim_jB_j$; the symbol $A_j$ in the conclusion means this coefficient sheaf when used in a sheaf tensor product. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a domain and a principal ideal ring, hence Noetherian (each ideal has one generator). Multiplication by $\varpi^n$ is injective on the discrete constant $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf: a section is locally represented by constants, and its product can vanish only if those constants vanish. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] with $I=(\varpi)$: $R$ is flat over that constant sheaf and $R/\varpi^nR=B_n$. Tensoring the injective multiplication map with this flat sheaf proves that $\varpi^n:R\to R$ is injective. Thus $K_n=[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R]$, in degrees $[-1,0]$, with degree-zero augmentation to $B_n$, is a bounded free resolution. It is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]: tensoring an acyclic complex with $K_n$ gives a shifted cone of multiplication by $\varpi^n$, which is acyclic by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact].

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat; elementary one-generator Koszul resolution

proof.text: First realize the finite-coefficient transitions by strict complexes, rather than choosing unrelated cones in $D(R)$. Choose a K-flat complex $Q_1$ with flat terms representing $M_1$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Inductively suppose $Q_j$ and its identification with $M_j$ are chosen. Choose a representative $C_{j+1}$ of $M_{j+1}$. In $D(B_{j+1})$ the prescribed transition to $\operatorname{Res}_{j+1,j}Q_j$ is a right fraction, by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]: it is represented by a roof $C_{j+1}\leftarrow Z\to\operatorname{Res}_{j+1,j}Q_j$ with the left map a quasi-isomorphism. Replace $Z$ by a K-flat resolution with flat terms and compose the right chain map. Call the resulting complex $Q_{j+1}$. This constructs a strict semilinear chain map $Q_{j+1}\to Q_j$ representing the prescribed transition, while preserving all previously chosen levels. Define longer transitions by composition. The cocycle in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] says that these represent every $\tau_{m,n}$. After restriction to $R$ this is an object of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_R(X))$. Its level identifications with the given coherent $R$-tower commute with transitions; [lem-weil-pbc-sequential-tower-evaluation-full] lifts them to an isomorphism of derived towers. Hence it suffices to prove the assertion for this strict model, using its Roos limit and its projections, and then transport by that isomorphism. No uniqueness of this lift is needed.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic (right fractions); Tag 06YS in sites-cohomology.tex (K-flat resolutions); explicit successor induction

proof.text: Fix $n$ and retain the tail $m\geq n$. In the strict Roos cone of [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle], the discarded finite initial factors occur with identity diagonal blocks in $1-s$. Successively eliminating the first coordinate removes a contractible identity cone; the inverse extension of a tail element to an earlier coordinate is its transition image. Thus removing this finite prefix preserves the limit and its projections on the tail. Tensoring $K_n$ with $B_m$ gives $C_{m,n}=[B_m\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_m]$. Its augmentation $\epsilon_{m,n}:C_{m,n}\to B_n$ is coefficient reduction in degree zero. The kernel of multiplication by $\varpi^n$ is $\varpi^{m-n}B_m$, identified with $B_n$ by $\bar a\mapsto\varpi^{m-n}a$; the kernel and cokernel statements follow by divisibility in the DVR, locally on constant sections. Set $F_{m,n}=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_{m,n})[-1]$ using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its only cohomology is that kernel in degree $-1$. The chain map $B_n[1]\to F_{m,n}$ inserting $\varpi^{m-n}\bar a$ in the degree-$-1$ component of $C_{m,n}$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Under reduction $m'\to m$, it satisfies the strict identity $q_{m',m}(\varpi^{m'-n}a)=\varpi^{m'-m}\varpi^{m-n}q_{m',m}(a)$. Consequently these fiber identifications commute with transitions when the source copies of $B_n[1]$ have transition multiplication by $\varpi^{m'-m}$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: coefficient complex, augmentation fiber and transition calculation; strict cone expanded

proof.text: Tensor these strict coefficient cones with $Q_m$ over $B_m$. This preserves the quasi-isomorphism just constructed because $Q_m$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]; explicitly, the cone of a quasi-isomorphism is acyclic, and its tensor with $Q_m$ is the cone of the tensor map, with the signs of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The same signed cone formula shows that tensoring the coefficient triangle gives a triangle of strict towers after restriction to $R$. Its middle tower is $T_m=Q_m\otimes_R K_n$, and its right tower is $S_m=Q_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n$. For example the reassociation between $Q_m\otimes_{B_m}(B_m\otimes_RK_n)$ and $Q_m\otimes_RK_n$ sends $q\otimes(b\otimes k)$ to $bq\otimes k$, with inverse $q\otimes k\mapsto q\otimes(1\otimes k)$; these formulas preserve degrees, differentials and semilinear transitions. Thus this is a complex-level reassociation, not an assertion about ordinary tensor preserving arbitrary exact sequences. The left tower is quasi-isomorphic to $S_m[1]$ with transitions $\varpi^{m'-m}$ times those of $S$. In particular its $n$ successive transitions are strictly zero. The maps $S_m\to Q_n$ induced by the strict transitions are the adjoint normalization maps and are quasi-isomorphisms by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. They form a strict map $S_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}(Q_n)$, since the transitions were defined by composition.

source.place: Proof, second and third paragraphs: tensor coefficient triangles and use normalization; strict semilinear maps supplied by step 2

proof.text: In the Roos triangle [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] for the left tower, its shift endomorphism $s$ has $s^n=0$, since each component of $s^n$ is an $n$-fold transition. Hence $(1-s)^{-1}=1+s+\cdots+s^{n-1}$ by multiplying out, and its Roos cone is zero. The exact derived inverse limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] therefore sends the tower triangle to an isomorphism $R\lim T_m\to R\lim S_m$. The strict levelwise quasi-isomorphism $S_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}(Q_n)$ identifies the latter limit with $Q_n$. Here the constant-tower identification is explicit: on any termwise product of a complex $Q$, the map $(x_m)\mapsto(x_m-x_{m+1})$ is degreewise split surjective, with a preimage of $(y_m)$ given by $x_n=0$ and $x_{n+r}=-\sum_{j=n}^{n+r-1}y_j$; its kernel is the diagonal $Q$. These maps commute with differentials and give the cone quasi-isomorphism from $Q$ with its diagonal projections.

source.place: Proof, fourth paragraph: nilpotent fiber tower and limits; constant tower calculation expanded

proof.text: By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], all the derived products in this calculation are termwise products of the strict complexes. Tensoring with the two-term free $K_n$ commutes with those products: in degree $r$ both sides are $(\prod_m Q_m^r)\oplus(\prod_m Q_m^{r+1})$, with identical differentials and transition endomorphisms. It also commutes with the Roos cone, because the cone involves only shifts and two-term sums and the total tensor differential has the signs of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This gives $M\otimes_R^LB_n\cong R\lim_m(Q_m\otimes_RK_n)=R\lim_mT_m$ after restricting the left side to $R$. The finite direct sums in this calculation allow arbitrary unbounded $Q_m$; there is no exchange of products with infinite tensor totalizations. Combined with step 5 this proves that the comparison to $M_n$ is an isomorphism on underlying $R$-complexes. For the completed-coefficient map $\pi_n:R\to B_n$, the ordinary tensor-restriction adjunction sends $f:N\to\operatorname{Res}_nP$ to $x\otimes b\mapsto bf(x)$, with inverse $g\mapsto(x\mapsto g(x\otimes1))$. Balancing verifies these inverse maps. Restriction is exact because it keeps the underlying abelian sheaf, so its termwise functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes its right derived functor. Derived extension along $\pi_n$ is everywhere defined by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Thus [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] applies and gives $-\otimes_R^LB_n\dashv\operatorname{Res}_n$. The comparison itself is in $D(B_n)$, as the adjoint of the $n$-th limit projection under this adjunction. Restriction of scalars leaves all underlying kernels and cokernels unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so it detects acyclic cones and hence detects isomorphisms. The comparison is therefore an isomorphism in $D(B_n)$.

source.place: Proof, fourth paragraph: bounded finite-free resolution commutes with derived products and the Roos cone

proof.text: These are the counit comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms: the map in step 5 is induced by $Q_m\otimes_RK_n\to Q_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n\to Q_n$, whose adjoint is the original strict transition to level $n$, and step 6 carries it to the adjoint of the limit projection. For $n\geq k$, composing that projection with $\tau_{n,k}$ gives the projection to $k$. The completed-coefficient tensor-restriction adjunction of step 6 [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] and the quotient cocycle of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] therefore identify the reduction of the $n$-th comparison with the $k$-th comparison; equality of adjoints proves the equality of these maps. At the strict coefficient resolution level the quotient $B_n\to B_k$ is represented by $K_n\to K_k$ with components $(\varpi^{n-k},1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$, since $\varpi^k\varpi^{n-k}=\varpi^n$; these maps compose strictly. Thus the comparison family intertwines the original tower with the quotient tower of $M$, including its maps from $M$. Transporting the Roos triangle along these isomorphisms makes $M\to\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_n(M\otimes_R^LB_n)$ the first map of a distinguished triangle completing $1-s$. This is precisely the condition of [def-weil-derived-complete]. The extra coefficient-object paragraph of the imported proof is unnecessary for the stated assertion and is not used.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: counit compatibility and derived completeness; irrelevant coefficient-object assertion omitted

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported coefficient-fiber proof into seven steps using only existing nodes. Supplied strict finite-coefficient representatives by successive roofs and K-flat replacement, related them to the given R-tower by evaluation fullness, proved uniform fiber nilpotence, and explicitly commuted the two-term free resolution with products and Roos cones. Preserved the statement and excluded boundedness or constructibility hypotheses. No new nodes. Maintainer-reader citation repair: explicitly derive the completed-coefficient tensor-restriction adjunction from lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors, exact restriction, and everywhere-defined derived change of rings, rather than attributing it to the finite-level adjunction in the tower definition.

The additional coefficient-object completeness paragraph is not needed by this item.
